text:
sandra: heads-up — customer hitting intermittent 503s when we cut over to private endpoints. error rate spikes for a few minutes then recovers. appears during cert rotation window and large reconnect fanout. anyone seen this pattern?

ajay: can you paste a snippet of connector logs / conn counts when it happens?

sandra: pasted a trimmed log below — timestamps line up with the cutover event:

```
2026-03-22T14:01:11Z ERROR connector=tenant-123 accept error: accept tcp 10.10.4.2:8443: accept: too many open files
2026-03-22T14:01:12Z WARN  connector=tenant-123 controlplane: reconnecting (attempt 1)
2026-03-22T14:01:12Z WARN  connector=tenant-456 controlplane: reconnecting (attempt 1)
2026-03-22T14:01:12Z ERROR connector=tenant-789 http: TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-03-22T14:01:13Z ERROR controlplane broker: dial tcp 100.64.0.5:443: i/o timeout
```

devon: that looks like a classic reconnect storm + file-descriptor exhaustion. when certs rotate we currently nuke and re-open all streams concurrently. we don't have jitter/backoff across tenants.

lina: confirmed. current operator flow sends a broadcast restart and each connector immediately re-dials control plane. no coordination.

ajay: two levels of fixes:
- short-term: add client-side jitter + exponential backoff and limit concurrent dialers per process (token bucket). also increase accept backlog and FD ulimit temporarily.
- med-term: edge-level backpressure: if connector queue (pending requests) > threshold then return 429/retry advice to customer, or throttle reconnection bursts.

mike: long-term we should avoid global fanout for cert refresh. options:
1) staged cert roll (per-region / per-tenant waves),
2) make controlplane do graceful handshakes: keep old cert valid for X minutes and allow overlapping handshakes,
3) move to a subscription model where connectors poll for rotation metadata and apply per-connector windows.

lina: also worth noting our current cert refresh triggers full TLS rehandshake even for long-lived tunnels (we re-establish TCP). could we support TLS rekey without full TCP reconnect? that's a bigger change but would reduce blast radius.

ajay: +1. another immediate mitigation is to add an outbound circuit-breaker so controlplane side can say "slow down" and connectors will backoff with jitter. we already expose health signalling but not a rate-control channel.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out connector-backoff-2026-03-22 to staging (canary: tenant-100). Logs show reduced reconnect concurrency by ~70%.

sandra: nice. proposed action items:
- lina: draft lightweight RFC for "staggered cert rotation" + operator changes (include rollout playbook and metrics).
- ajay: implement token-bucket dial limiter and jittered backoff in connector (short patch).
- devon: run FD and backlog tuning in staging + monitor acceptance errors.
- mike: investigate TLS rekey feasibility and add to roadmap.

lina: :raised_hands: I'll take the RFC. will include a small section on fallbacks (circuit-breaker and 429 semantics) and a test plan.

sandra: thanks — please post RFC link here when ready so we can triage for next release. for immediate ops: ajay & devon, can you coordinate a small hotfix this week?

ajay: yes, will open PR tonight and tag @devon.

mike: ping me once staging shows the canary behaving for 24h, I'll sign off on promoting to prod.

sandra: perfect. closing the loop here — i'll create a short incident log and link to the RFC once it's drafted. :thumbsup:
